evaluation.detected_misconception: Assuming the list always contains at least one positive number.
evaluation.feedback: You correctly spotted that the starting value 0 causes a problem when every number is negative. Good job explaining that the function then returns 0, which is not in the list. For full marks, also describe what happens with an empty list.
evaluation.practice_tip: When you look for the largest or smallest element, start from the first element of the list, not from an arbitrary constant.

evaluation.detected_misconception: Assuming it is safe to remove elements from the list the loop is currently iterating over.
evaluation.feedback: You correctly spotted that numbers.remove inside the loop causes the problem and that the next element gets skipped because of it. The example with two negative numbers next to each other is a good one. For full marks, also explain why the elements shift to the left.
evaluation.practice_tip: When you drop elements from a list, build a new list with the ones you keep instead of changing the list the loop is iterating over.

hints: Does the function work for every order of numbers in the list, or only for some?

evaluation.detected_misconception: Assuming the search can stop as soon as low and high become equal.
evaluation.feedback: You correctly spotted that the while loop condition ends the search too early. Good job giving an example with the target at the end of the list. For full marks, also explain what happens with a list of one element.
evaluation.practice_tip: For every loop, check what happens at the boundary: when exactly one candidate is left, does the loop still check it?
